title: Five countries pledge troops for the International Stabilization Force in Gaza
body:
On Thursday 19 February 2026, at a Board of Peace meeting in Washington, US Army General Jasper Jeffers, head of the planned International Stabilization Force for Gaza, announced that five countries would send troops. Al Jazeera reported that Indonesia, Kazakhstan, Morocco, Kosovo and Albania had made pledges. Indonesia's President Prabowo Subianto said his country would provide up to 8,000 personnel, and Jeffers said Indonesia had accepted the position of deputy commander.

Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev said his country would send an unspecified number of personnel, including medical units, and Morocco's Foreign Minister Nasser Bourita said Morocco was ready to deploy police officers. No figures were given for Kosovo or Albania. Egypt and Jordan were to train police officers rather than deploy troops. Indonesia's foreign ministry described its mission as humanitarian, focused on civilian protection, health aid, reconstruction and training Palestinian police, and said its troops would not be involved in combat operations.

Usman Hamid, head of Amnesty International Indonesia, warned that participation could risk joining a mechanism that strengthens violations of international humanitarian law, and Palestinians voiced concern that the board would entrench Israel's occupation. Al Jazeera cited a Gaza death toll of at least 72,000 and said almost 600 Palestinians had been killed in Israeli attacks during the ceasefire with Hamas.
